text:
alex: Quick heads-up — onboarding an HF chat model and the HF->Redwood conversion step is nuking the system block when the original chat_template uses Jinja conditionals. Repro attached below, looks like curly braces/escape handling + tokenizer differences. Anyone seen this?

maria: can you paste the problematic template snippet?

alex: sure, minimal example: 
```jinja
{% if persona %}
<|system|>You are a helpful, terse assistant for {{ persona }}.
{% endif %}
<|user|>{{ user_input }}</|user|>
```

alex: After conversion the runtime prompt becomes: `You are a helpful, terse assistant for .\n{{ user_input }}` — system role gone, braces still visible in places.

sam.k: ugh, that's the classic Jinja vs literal-brace problem. Are we running the template renderer before or after tokenization?

alex: renderer runs in our HF->RW converter which is python-based. We call Template.render(...) then assemble Redwood prompt pieces. But when persona is falsy we still end up with stray markers because HF had role markers as tokens rather than separate message entries.

lee: could be two issues: 1) HF chat_template encodes role wrappers as special tokens (eg ``<|system|>``) that the tokenizer sometimes splits during quantized inference; 2) our conversion script treats those wrappers as plain text and does naive regex replace for braces.

maria: also saw this: some HF templates rely on `{%-` trimming and whitespace control; if we drop those characters earlier we change token boundaries which breaks eval prompts.

alex: timeline: brought model up on dedicated, ran eval harness (SMOKE-qa) and saw a 6-8% hit on system-prompt-sensitive tasks. Narrowed down to a subset of test cases where template had conditionals/loops.

sam.k: quick patch idea: do explicit AST parse of the chat_template instead of raw render+replace. Keep role-segmented messages as array elements and convert each to Redwood block. That preserves role separation.

lee: yeah — treat role tokens as structural. Eg convert HF chat_template entries to list: [ {role: "system", content: "..."}, {role: "user", content: "..."} ] and then stringify for Redwood. Avoid interpolating unrendered braces into final string.

maria: small repro script (pseudo):
```py
from jinja2 import Environment
env = Environment()
tmpl = env.from_string(hf_template)
rendered = tmpl.render(**ctx)
# BAD: re.sub(r"<\|system\|>.*?<\|/system\|>", "", rendered)
# GOOD: parse into messages first, then render each content separately and join with separators
```

alex: thanks. two open questions: 1) tokenizer divergence — do we need to apply the HF tokenizer pre-conversion to detect token splits for special tokens? 2) unit tests: how do we assert parity after conversion?

sam.k: for 1) yes, run HF tokenizer on the original template pieces to detect if any special tokens are being split into subtokens. If so, add a pre-token mapping or update special_tokens_map before model bring-up.

lee: for 2) add a tiny regression suite that renders N canonical templates with edge cases (conditional, loop, escape sequences, whitespace control) and compare (a) Redwood-assembled prompt tokens (post-conversion) and (b) HF raw-rendered tokens. Fail if mismatch on role boundaries or if system role disappears. Keep tests lightweight and run in CI with emulators.

alex: one weirdness: with 4-bit quant on the runtime we sometimes see decoder join tokens differently during sampling which made golden exact-token-match tests flaky. Any tips?

maria: don't assert exact token ids for quantized runs; instead assert role-presence and normalized string contains key phrases. Eg assert system prompt substring present and that user content appears after system marker. Use fuzzy equality (levenshtein <= 2) for quantized smoke.

sam.k: also log the tokenization offsets during conversion in a short map so operators can inspect which bytes -> tokens changed. That helped us debug a previous model where `<|endoftext|>` got merged into adjacent text due to tokenizer config differences.

ci-bot: deploy queued by @alex for branch hf-template-fix. CI will run eng-ml/regression/templates (5 jobs).

alex: thanks all — I'll do the AST approach and add the small regression set. Will ping when PR is up. If anyone has quick snippets to detect split special tokens with huggingface tokenizers, send them here. :pray:
